assets.alt: Layered FastAPI generative AI service with API routers, controls, and data-source integrations connected to models, a database, and external applications.
assets.caption: The service boundary coordinates HTTP controls, models, persistence, and third-party integrations without collapsing them into one layer.

assets.alt: An event loop receives requests from four clients, delegates work to workers, and routes callbacks and responses back to each client.
assets.caption: The event loop keeps many requests moving by delegating work and resuming each request when its result is ready.

assets.alt: Nested comparison of RBAC, ReBAC, and ABAC using roles, team relationships, and subscription attributes to control access to text and image models.
assets.caption: RBAC grants by role, ReBAC by relationship, and ABAC by attributes such as subscription tier.

assets.alt: Sequence diagrams comparing HTTP request-response, short polling, long polling, server-sent events, and bidirectional WebSocket communication.
assets.caption: Choose a communication pattern by update direction, latency needs, and connection lifetime—not by novelty.

assets.alt: Nested boxes showing multiprocessing parallelism as one way to execute work within the broader concept of concurrency, which also includes threading and async I/O.
assets.caption: Concurrency coordinates overlapping work; parallelism executes work simultaneously, often across processes.

assets.alt: Side-by-side stacks showing virtual machines with a guest OS per application and containers sharing the host operating system while packaging their own libraries.
assets.caption: Containers share the host OS, while virtual machines package a separate guest OS for each workload.

assets.alt: A video-summary query sends an LLM a cache reference while files are stored once in a multimodal cache containing video, image, audio, and document content.
assets.caption: Context caching lets repeated requests reference previously uploaded multimodal content instead of resending it.

assets.alt: Two token grids showing continuous batching filling open sequence slots with new prompt tokens as other sequences emit output or stop tokens.
assets.caption: Continuous batching replaces finished sequences immediately, keeping more accelerator slots productive.

assets.alt: Layer diagram showing a controller calling services that use a repository and database, and providers that connect to email, GitHub, and other external applications.
assets.caption: Controllers coordinate use cases; repositories isolate persistence, and providers isolate external systems.

assets.alt: FastAPI service architecture with API routers and authentication guards, modality-specific resource controllers, shared services, storage systems, and text, image, video, audio, geometry, and embedding models.
assets.caption: A modular AI service can expose many modalities while keeping routing, resource control, services, storage, and models separate.

assets.alt: Dependency graph where get_db feeds get_user, and get_user feeds both a user endpoint and get_user_message for a messages endpoint.
assets.caption: FastAPI resolves shared dependencies as a graph, reusing upstream results across endpoint-specific logic.

assets.alt: Docker client commands communicate with the Docker daemon, which builds and runs containers from images pulled from a registry.
assets.caption: The Docker client directs the daemon, while registries distribute the images from which containers run.

assets.alt: RAG pipeline from file upload through extraction, transformation, vector storage, retrieval, and generation, overlaid with separate upload, generation, and full-workflow end-to-end test boundaries.
assets.caption: End-to-end tests should cover both individual API workflows and the complete upload-to-answer path.

assets.alt: A client calls a FastAPI service that asks separate authorization logic to decide an actor-resource-action tuple, then enforces the allow or deny result.
assets.caption: Keep policy decisions separate from enforcement: the authorization service decides, and the API applies the result.

assets.alt: Comparison of a direct prompt-to-LLM path with a guarded path that checks inputs for PII, off-topic requests, and jailbreaks and checks outputs for hallucinations, profanity, and competitor mentions.
assets.caption: Guardrails constrain both sides of the model boundary: unsafe inputs before inference and unacceptable outputs afterward.

assets.alt: Docker host with two separate bridge networks, docker0 and genai-net, each assigning its own subnet addresses to connected containers.
assets.caption: Separate bridge networks create explicit connectivity boundaries between groups of containers.

assets.alt: FastAPI authentication architecture showing login, registration, and password reset routes, password and token services, user persistence, token issuance, and token-protected resource requests.
assets.caption: Authentication verifies credentials and issues tokens; protected resource routes validate those tokens on later requests.

assets.alt: A model-loading timeline showing a generative model loaded from disk into memory during a request, used for inference, and then unloaded after that request.
assets.caption: Loading a model inside every request repeats expensive disk-to-memory work and makes latency unpredictable.

assets.alt: Application lifespan timeline showing a generative model loaded from disk into RAM at startup, reused for each inference request, and unloaded only after the shutdown signal.
assets.caption: FastAPI lifespan loads the model once, reuses it across requests, and releases it during shutdown.

assets.alt: OAuth authorization-code flow where a client requests consent and scopes, exchanges the returned grant code for an access token, and uses the token to call a resource server.
assets.caption: OAuth keeps resource-owner consent, token issuance, and protected-resource access as distinct steps.

assets.alt: Concentric application layers with models and repositories at the center, services, providers, and dependencies around them, and controllers, routers, guards, mappers, and exception filters at the edge.
assets.caption: Onion architecture keeps domain and persistence abstractions inside, with transport and framework concerns at the edge.

assets.alt: Side-by-side diagrams of a token bucket that admits traffic when tokens are available and a leaky bucket that emits packets at a constant rate and drops overflow.
assets.caption: Token buckets permit controlled bursts; leaky buckets smooth output to a steady rate and discard overflow.

assets.alt: Onion architecture with repositories beside models in the center, separating database access from services and outer transport concerns.
assets.caption: Repositories keep persistence details behind an inner interface that services can use without depending on the database implementation.

assets.alt: Sequence diagram showing an HTTP handshake and acknowledgment followed by a one-way stream of server-sent messages from server to client.
assets.caption: Server-sent events use one persistent HTTP connection for server-to-client updates.

assets.alt: A container connected to three storage choices on the host: a bind mount in the host filesystem, a Docker-managed volume, and an in-memory tmpfs mount.
assets.caption: Bind mounts, managed volumes, and tmpfs provide different persistence, ownership, and lifecycle trade-offs.

assets.alt: Three testing scopes: unit tests isolate small code units, integration tests connect code to services or databases, and end-to-end tests exercise a user flow across multiple services.
assets.caption: Unit, integration, and end-to-end tests trade isolation for progressively broader system confidence.

assets.alt: Inheritance-style diagram showing fake, dummy, stub, spy, and mock as specialized forms of the general test-double concept.
assets.caption: Fakes, dummies, stubs, spies, and mocks replace collaborators for different testing purposes.

assets.alt: Timeline comparing serial single-threaded requests, multithreaded requests that alternate CPU ownership under the GIL, and asyncio requests that overlap while waiting for I/O.
assets.caption: Threads and asyncio both overlap I/O waits, but they schedule work through different execution models.

assets.alt: Before-and-after traffic plots showing irregular bursts buffered into an ordered queue and released at a stable target rate.
assets.caption: Traffic shaping absorbs bursts and releases work near a target rate that downstream capacity can sustain.

assets.alt: Sequence diagram showing a client opening GET /ws, completing an HTTP handshake with the server, and then exchanging bidirectional messages.
assets.caption: A WebSocket begins with an HTTP upgrade and then supports messages in both directions over one connection.

assets.alt: WebSocket lifecycle from connecting through the HTTP upgrade and 101 response, to bidirectional data frames in the open state, close frames, and TCP termination.
assets.caption: The WebSocket lifecycle has explicit upgrade, open data-transfer, closing-handshake, and closed states.
